subject.title: Google Chat: markdown renders as raw text; typing indicator says 'OpenClaw is typing' instead of app name

question: Should Google Chat convert assistant Markdown into Google Chat-supported markup, strip unsupported Markdown to plain text, or keep the current markdown-capable contract and narrow this issue to the typing-name bug?
rationale: Current source marks Google Chat as markdown-capable, the issue asks for strip or conversion behavior, and a related PR discussion challenged the premise that Google Chat cannot render markdown; automation should not choose the permanent channel rendering contract.

options.title: Convert supported markup
options.body: Add a Google Chat renderer that maps common assistant Markdown into the Google Chat dialect, strips unsupported markers, and also fixes the `agent.identity.name` typing fallback.

options.title: Plain text only
options.body: Treat Google Chat as plain text by stripping Markdown and updating metadata, docs, and tests to remove the current markdown-capable contract.

options.title: Typing fix only
options.body: Fix the display-name fallback and explicitly document that Google Chat remains markdown-capable without a bespoke dialect converter.

recommendation.title: Convert supported markup
recommendation.body: Add a Google Chat renderer that maps common assistant Markdown into the Google Chat dialect, strips unsupported markers, and also fixes the `agent.identity.name` typing fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current routing signal from Google Chat introduction, typing-message commit history, and later reply-delivery refactors.
